ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a plate schematic diagram centered near Southeast Asia—Australia, and there are multiple curved plate boundary lines within the circle. A is located in the upper left part of the figure, near the Asian continent; B is located on the left side, slightly toward the middle, near an island arc; C and D are both located from the lower right of the figure to Australia and the adjacent Indian Ocean area. In the figure, there is no plate boundary line separating C and D from each other, while there are boundary lines separating A and B from other places respectively. Then reason: To judge whether they are located on the same plate, one must see whether the two places are separated by a plate boundary. A and B are respectively in areas separated by different boundaries; C and D are located in the same continuous plate area of Australia and its adjacent Indian Ocean area, so the ones located on the same plate are C and D.
